_howto: Add entries below. type: video | image | code. Put files in assets/work/<section>/. For video give src (mp4/webm) and poster (jpg/png). For code give lang + code (use \n for line breaks).

vfx.title: Ultimate and cooldowns
vfx.text: An ultimate cast read end to end: rings opening on the ground, damage numbers off every target caught in them, and the cooldown draining on the bar in the same frame.

vfx.title: Lightning strike
vfx.text: A column that lands from above: flash, bolt, and a ring of dust that outlives it by a beat so the hit reads even at a distance.

vfx.title: Solar strike
vfx.text: Charge, flash, shockwave. The core is a single neon shape carrying the light — everything else around it is particles that fade from the impact point outward.

vfx.title: Void rift
vfx.text: The cast recolours the whole scene: the sky shifts, the ground goes violet, and the tear itself is layered parts and beams rather than a flat texture.

models.title: Winged monument
models.text: Paired feathered wings over a fluted column, gold banding and lit panels around the base. Built as a landmark rather than a prop — it has to read from across the hub, not up close.

models.title: Training dummy
models.text: A padded post with a target roundel and frost spikes on a weighted base. It stands in the training ground and has to survive being hit from any angle, so it reads the same from all sides.

scripting.title: Procedural dungeon
scripting.text: Rooms are drawn per door from a weighted template pool and stitched at run time, so no two runs share a floor plan. The generator owns the layout, the props and the spawns, then hands a finished floor to the gameplay services.

scripting.title: Boss fight
scripting.text: Phase timers, telegraphed attacks and a health bar the server owns. The client renders what the server has already decided, and the run ends in the reward window you see at the end of the clip.

scripting.title: Live monument
scripting.text: A world object wired to live player data: the panel is a real view of saved stats, redrawn as they change, not a decorative prop with numbers painted on.

scripting.title: Leaderboard
scripting.text: Standings ordered on the server, capped, and written to a board in the world. It refreshes in place — no rejoin, no reload.

scripting.title: Upgrade altar
scripting.text: A node tree where every node is a real upgrade record. What you can afford lights up, what you cannot stays dim, and the server checks the same table before it grants anything.

scripting.title: Forge window
scripting.text: Components on the left, the result previewed live on the right. Every field is driven by the same recipe table the server validates against, so the preview cannot promise something the craft will refuse.

scripting.title: Inventory
scripting.text: Tabs for gear and materials over forty dynamic slots, with counts read straight from the saved profile.

scripting.title: Dungeon menu
scripting.text: Pick a floor before you go in: unlock rules, saved progress and the reward line for each one, all read from the same config the generator builds against.

scripting.title: Radial menu
scripting.text: One ring, six destinations. Keyboard and mouse land on the same handler, so the menu behaves identically whichever you use.

scripting.title: Admin panel and levelling
scripting.text: A gated panel that grants XP, coins and items for testing — sitting on top of the same levelling service a player progresses through, so what it hands out follows the real rules.

scripting.title: Station prompts
scripting.text: Every station in the world shares one prompt system: proximity, hold-to-use and a per-station accent colour. Adding a station is a table entry, not new code.

scripting.title: Breakables
scripting.text: Destructible props that pay out. Hits are resolved on the server, the payout is rolled there too, and each object carries its own respawn timer.

scripting.title: Loading screen
scripting.text: It covers the teleport into a floor and owns the whole hand-off — fade, hints, and the moment control comes back — so the player never sees a half-built room.

characters.title: Blacksmith
characters.text: The forge keeper: leather apron over rolled sleeves, one shoulder plated, one bare. Built on the standard rig, so every animation the player characters use works on him unchanged.

characters.title: Wizard
characters.text: Robe, pointed hat and a crystal staff, with an orb resting in the open hand and a rune ring turning at his feet. The staff head and the ring are the only lit materials on him — everything else is flat colour.

world.title: The map
world.text: Everything above the water in one frame: a central hub with three themed islands hung off it, each on its own bridge. Nothing is procedural — the layout is placed by hand so the sightlines from the hub centre land on every landmark.

world.title: Central hub
world.text: Radial paving that reads as a compass from the air: every path from the rim lands on the ring at the centre, and the four bridge heads sit on the axes.

world.title: Portal island
world.text: Deep blue slate, standing stones and a lit vortex on the platform. The blue channel of the bridge carries the same palette across so the island reads before you arrive.

world.title: Magma island
world.text: Basalt terraces with lava channels cut into them, braziers on the rim and broken rock floating under the underside. The hottest colour on the map, kept to one island on purpose.

world.title: Worldtree island
world.text: One tree carries the whole silhouette: the island underneath is deliberately small and plain so the canopy is what you see from the hub.
